title: Fleet Manager: SLA-backed scaling presets, throughput targets, and audit timeline in Console
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a unified Fleet Manager view in the Redwood Console that lets customers define SLA-backed throughput targets, apply scaling presets across fleets, view fine-grained throughput dashboards, and inspect a tamper-evident change history (audit timeline). This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the Console UX and API surface necessary to ship scaling controls tied to throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create and save scaling presets (preset = desired min/max GPU capacity, target tokens/sec, and cooldown windows) and apply them to one or more fleets from the Fleet Manager UI.
A new throughput dashboard is available per fleet showing: 1m/5m/15m tokens/sec, 95th percentile latency, current active workers, and autoscaler decisions with timestamps for the last 7 days.

SLA mode: customers can set a throughput SLA (tokens/sec) and a cost-priority toggle (cost-first | performance-first). The system surfaces expected commit cost delta and fallback policies before changes are saved.

Change history (audit timeline) captures: who made the change, change type (preset apply/edit/remove, SLA update, manual scale), previous and new values, and an immutable timestamp. Timeline supports filter by actor and change type and is downloadable as CSV.

Console writes configuration changes to the control-plane API; changes are validated and rejected if they violate account-level capacity constraints. Validation errors are surfaced inline in the UI with suggested remediation steps.
Backend API endpoints follow the existing Console contracts and pass E2E smoke tests; front-end components are feature-flagged behind 'fleet_manager_v2' for staged rollout.
Product and Eng have run a load test demonstrating autoscaler respects presets under 2x burst conditions without violating conservative latency targets. Test artifacts are linked in PRs and CI.
Security: audit timeline events are logged to customer audit logs and accessible via the Private control plane for Private customers. Security review signed off or flagged with mitigation steps.
design_notes: Design will reuse Console's route pattern and table components; new Fleet Manager page includes three panes: Fleet selector, throughput dashboard, and presets/timeline panel.
Visual signature: green SLA badge when current throughput >= target for configured window; amber when within 10% of target; red when below target for >5 minutes.
Mobile: initial release scoped to desktop only. Lightweight read-only mobile views planned for follow-up cycle.
Accessibility: all interactive elements must have keyboard focus and ARIA labels; timeline entries support screen-reader semantics.
implementation_notes: Backend: add endpoints POST /fleets/:id/presets and GET /fleets/:id/throughput with schema v2. Include change author metadata in create/update payloads.
Autoscaler: introduce 'preset' evaluation stage before decision commit; if preset conflicts with current batch scheduling rules, autoscaler returns a validation code for the Console to surface.
Data retention: throughput metrics aggregated at 1m granularity for last 30 days, 5m for 90 days. Timeline events retained per account retention policy (default 365 days).
Telemetry: emit events for preset create/edit/apply and SLA breaches to observability pipeline to power alerts and regression dashboards.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (feature-flagged beta): release to internal and 5 pilot Dedicated customers. Monitor cost deltas and false positives in validations for 2 weeks.
Phase 2: expand to all Dedicated customers in Hosted regions, enable read-only for Private until audit log integrations are validated.
Phase 3: enable full write capabilities in Private control plane after KMS and audit integration certification.
